messages.subject: Help factor loading CFA
parts:
Hi

Im really new into CFA and currently Im in a (steep) learning curve ;). 

So I have read already quite a bit (like http://www.understandingdata.net/2017/03/22/cfa-in-lavaan/) and I have a working model. However I wonder how I load the factor correctly.

I am trying to produce a factor / latent variable called metabolic load which comprise of 6 metabolic variabeles which are visceral fat (VAT), subcuteanous fat (SAT), HDL, Tryglicerides (TG), Glucose (GLUC) and blood pressure (BP) 

From https://stackoverflow.com/questions/22024700/how-can-i-extract-factor-loadings-from-lavaan I understand that I get the loading of each variable on the factor by using inspect(fit,what="std")$lambda.

I get the following matrice but its without p-values:

> inspect(model,what="std")

education  0.000      0      0      0    0      0      0    1



Morever from here https://www.researchgate.net/post/What_is_the_acceptable_range_for_factor_loading_in_SEM I understand that you dont necessarily have to load the factor according to this way, as long as the theoratical model is sound (which is ;)

So, whats the way to go?

Btw a nice example is this paper where they do the same thing (producing a latent variabel called metabolic load the same as I am doing: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6291122/) where they exluded blood pressure:

The selected indicators loaded significantly on the metabolic load factor (standardized estimates of path loadings: waist = .194; HDL = -.551, TG = .789; BZP1 = .366; p< .05) except systolic and diastolic blood pressure (standardized estimates of path loadings for RRsys: .038; RRdiast = .039 p >.200),

This is my full code btw, I will use the latent variable metabolic load as a mediator in the end between physical activity and cardiac function (confounders age, sex, smoking, ethnicity, education)

model <- ' # direct effect
cardiacf ~ c*physicala + age + sex + smoking + ethnicity + education

metaload =~ VAT + SAT + HDL + TG + GLUC + BP

cardiacf ~ b*metaload + age + sexe + smoking + ethnicity + eduh

meta ~ a*physicala 

# indirect effect (a*b)
ab := a*b


# direct
direff := c

# total effect
total := direff + ab

# pct mediated
med1 := 100*ab / total
'

I think you are looking for the summary() function:

summary(fit)

or if you prefer a data.frame:

parameterEstimates(fit)

Yves.

Great yes indeed!

Ok so I got his table, how do I select which variables actually load the factor 'meta' properly?

Here they say that any variable <0.7 should be excluded from the factor but doesnt need to be https://www.theanalysisfactor.com/factor-analysis-5/

As a rule of thumb, your variable should have a rotated factor loading of at least |0.4| (meaning ≥ +.4 or ≤ –.4) onto one of the factors in order to be considered important.

Some researchers use much more stringent criteria such as a cut-off of |0.7|. In some instances, this may not be realistic: for example, when the highest loading a researcher finds in her analysis is |0.5|.

Other researchers relax the criteria to the point where they include variables with factor loadings of |0.2|. Which cut-offs to use depends on whether you are running a confirmatory or exploratory factor analysis, and on what is usually considered an acceptable cut-off in your field. In addition, a variable should ideally only load cleanly onto one factor


However I understand from the table that all variables load the factor significantly (?). Moreover as long as the theory and assumptions are sound, all variables should be included?

You aren't adding a couple, you are adding all possible covariances between indicators.
I get errors which I dont rally understand

As the message suggests, your model is not identified.  It cannot be, because you have negative degrees of freedom.  An introductory SEM textbook could help explain why.
